"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 832.

What it does: this component is silent on ordinary text and loud on the
chat-format markers the model was trained with (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>,
<tool_call>, <tool_response>, <think> and their closing forms). Each marker
gets its typical level; the first token of every packed document is zero.
Ordinary tokens are predicted as zero.

The program reads only the newest token and the document labels, so it is
causal and keeps no state.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MARKER_LEVELS = {
    "<|im_start|>": 18.8,
    "<|im_end|>": 15.4,
    "<tool_call>": 15.0,
    "</tool_call>": 15.9,
    "<tool_response>": 20.0,
    "</tool_response>": 22.8,
    "<think>": 17.8,
    "</think>": 16.0,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or ids[t] != ids[t - 1]:
        return carry, 0.0  # first token of a document: the component is silent
    return carry, MARKER_LEVELS.get(prefix.token_strings[t], 0.0)

"""Layer 15 MLP neuron 833: this component is that neuron's output, scaled by a fixed norm.

What it responds to: the word itself, when the word is about copying, repeating,
duplicating or spreading something ("repeated", "copies", "copy", "replicate",
"spread", "widely", "worldwide", "translated"). Its output pushes the next-token
prediction toward words of the same kind ("copy", "copies", "replication",
"spread", "scaling"), so it is a copy/spread-word neuron.

This program predicts a fixed value on those words and 0 on every other token.
Measured on eval: variance explained is about 0.0005, and putting it in the model
does about what switching the component off does (kl_fraction 0.998). Most of the
activation is small, context-dependent noise on ordinary tokens (any token-level
or context-level feature I tried explains under 1%), and a word list cannot
capture it. A full 320-word table of token means reaches only about 0.004 on
held-out data, so no simple token rule captures much more.
"""

READS = ()

# Words about copying, repeating, duplicating or spreading things.
COPY_SPREAD = {
    "copy", "copies", "copied", "copying",
    "repeat", "repeated", "repeatedly", "repeating", "repeats",
    "duplicate", "duplicated", "replicate", "replicated", "replication",
    "spread", "spreading", "widespread", "widely", "worldwide",
    "translated", "scaled", "expanded", "twice",
}

VALUE = 1.2  # typical activation on these words; 0 on all other tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, (VALUE if word in COPY_SPREAD else 0.0)

"""Position-in-document profile of a weak, mostly unpredictable component.

The component (layer 15 MLP down-projection, unit 834) has a near-zero mean and a spread
of about 0.29 that no token identity or context concept explains. Its only reliable shape
is by position in its document: silent on a document's first token, a little positive
just after it, and smaller far into long documents.
"""

READS = ()

# mean activation by tokens since the document started (measured on training rows)
PROFILE = ((0, 0.0), (1, 0.03), (4, 0.07), (16, 0.05), (64, 0.02))


def _mean_at(pos):
    value = 0.0
    for start, mean in PROFILE:
        if pos >= start:
            value = mean
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    pos = 0 if new_doc else carry + 1
    return pos, _mean_at(pos)

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 835.

What it does, in plain terms: it is mostly quiet, and goes negative inside a noun
phrase that is still open, where the model is set up to name the head of the phrase,
especially a member of a group. Strongest cases: "some of the [people]", "all of the",
"the best [ways]", "the most [important]". Weakly positive when "the" starts a clause
("if the", "that the", "was the").

The program scores each token from its word class and the words just before it:
  - "the" after a quantifier + "of" ("some of the", "all of the")              -> strongly negative
  - "the" after "of" or another preposition ("in the", "for the")             -> negative
  - "the" after a clause word ("if the", "that the", "was the")                -> slightly positive
  - other "the"                                                               -> mildly negative
  - superlatives, ordinals and group-type adjectives ("best", "most", "first", "main")
                                                                             -> negative
  - an adjective after a determiner ("the [gray] shades"), or a noun after a
    preposition and a determiner ("in the [ribs]")                           -> mildly negative
  - other determiners and possessives ("our", "its", "these")  -> very mildly negative
Everything else predicts 0. Values are typical activations, in the component's own units.
"""

import wordnet

READS = ()

QUANTIFIERS = {"any", "some", "each", "many", "all", "most", "several", "both", "few",
               "none", "one", "two", "three", "half", "rest", "sum"}
PREPOSITIONS = {"of", "in", "to", "on", "for", "with", "from", "by", "at", "into",
                "between", "among", "through", "over", "under", "about", "during",
                "within", "around", "across", "against", "than", "as"}
CLAUSE_WORDS = {"if", "that", "is", "was", "when", "then", "but", "and", "or", ",", ".", ";"}
SUPERLATIVES = {"best", "most", "first", "main", "other", "different", "various",
                "favorite", "largest", "highest", "major", "early", "great", "big",
                "top", "earliest", "good", "old", "latest", "biggest"}
DETERMINERS = {"the", "a", "an", "our", "its", "your", "their", "my", "his", "her",
               "these", "those", "this", "every", "each", "all", "some", "any", "many",
               "several"}


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Only the newest three tokens matter; a document boundary counts as the start.
    words = [_word(s) for s in prefix.token_strings[-3:]]
    docs = prefix.document_ids[-3:]
    n = len(words)
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if docs[k] != docs[-1]:
            words[k] = ""
    cur = words[-1]
    prev = words[-2] if n >= 2 and docs[-2] == docs[-1] else ""
    prev2 = words[-3] if n >= 3 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] else ""
    det_near = prev in DETERMINERS or prev2 in DETERMINERS

    value = 0.0
    if cur == "the":
        if prev == "of" and prev2 in QUANTIFIERS:
            value = -2.0
        elif prev in PREPOSITIONS:
            value = -0.7
        elif prev in CLAUSE_WORDS or prev == "":
            value = 0.1
        else:
            value = -0.3
    elif cur in SUPERLATIVES:
        value = -0.8
    elif cur in DETERMINERS:
        value = -0.1
    elif cur.isalpha() and det_near and "adjective" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(cur):
        value = -0.2
    elif (cur.isalpha() and det_near and prev in PREPOSITIONS
          and "noun" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(cur)):
        value = -0.2
    return carry, float(value)

"""Baseline: predict the component's typical activation everywhere.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:836 is a single rank-one
readout of the layer-15 MLP's hidden units. Across ordinary text it has no
token-, position- or word-level pattern that a short rule can capture, so the
honest simple prediction is its average value, except at the first position of
a document, where it is essentially zero.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN = -0.022  # average activation over ordinary positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, MEAN

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 837: a "by" detector.

The component is mostly near zero, with a small diffuse wobble, but it spikes on the
word " by" when " by" introduces HOW something is done (a means or manner, usually
followed by a gerund): "reduce the greenhouse effect by reducing ...", "the data can be
downloaded by clicking ...", "allow for very fast ...". It is also high on " void" in
Java-style "public void ...", and mildly positive on words that announce a capability
or a means ("allows", "enables", "easy", "simple", "ability"). Those are the only
things this program predicts; everything else is 0.

Predicted values are the component's typical activations on the matching word:
" by" about 2.1 (its mean over 1000 rows, with a range from about -1 for math "divisible
by" to 8.8 for a clear means), " void" after "public" about 1.3, and about 0.7 for the
capability words.
"""

BY_VALUE = 2.1
VOID_VALUE = 1.3
CAPABILITY_VALUE = 0.7
CAPABILITY_WORDS = {" allows", " enables", " enable", " easy", " simple", " ability", " allow"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if word == " by":
        value = BY_VALUE
    elif word == " void":
        value = VOID_VALUE
    elif word in CAPABILITY_WORDS:
        value = CAPABILITY_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value


READS = ()

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:838: a near-silent, token-unpredictable direction.

What it does: its activation (the projection of layer 15's MLP hidden state onto this
component's read direction, times its write norm) is a small, dense, context-dependent
signal with std about 0.31 and no stable token preference. Token identity explains about
1% of its variance and the last few tokens together explain nothing held out, so no
short rule over the prefix predicts its value. Its switched-off effect on the model is
negligible (KL about 1.5e-6 nats per position).

So this program predicts the component's mean, which is about zero, at every position.
It is the honest simple version: it captures the (near-zero) mean and no more.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The activation is not predictable from the prefix's tokens, so predict its mean.
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-15 MLP down_proj component 840: a word-level guess at its activation.

The component's activation is mostly a dense, noisy signal (std about 0.4) that
no token, token pair, token class or position predicts (held-out R^2 near 0).
Its largest values (|activation| above 2) sit on a few kinds of word, with a
fairly consistent sign for each:
- positive on words that set one thing against another or mark a relation:
  than, against, versus/vs, despite, before, minus, whereas, opposed, and the
  Chinese/Japanese markers 被, 与, 跟, 给;
- negative on maths operators (x, *, *(, ^, mod, sin, d) and on verbs of
  knowing, learning or entering (learn, understand, know, knew, enter).

On every other token the program predicts 0. On held-out eval rows this
explains almost none of the variance (about 1e-4); it is a sign-only description
of the strongest word-driven spikes, not a model of the component.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CONTRAST = {"than", "against", "versus", "vs", "despite", "before", "minus", "whereas", "opposed", "被", "与", "跟", "给"}
MATHS = {"×", "*", "*(", "^", "mod", "sin", "∂"}
KNOWING = {"learn", "learned", "understand", "know", "knew", "knows", "enter", "entered"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word in CONTRAST:
        value = 0.5
    elif word in MATHS or word in KNOWING:
        value = -0.7
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Line-number gutter detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 843.

What it does, in plain terms: this component reads a listing that has line numbers
down its left edge, the way `cat -n` or an editor's view prints code ("   157<TAB>    code").
At the padding that starts each numbered line it fires strongly (about +7.7), since the
model is about to write the next line number there. It fires weakly (about +1) on the
digits of that line number. Everywhere else it stays near zero, with small offsets for
indentation that starts a line after a comment (+2.3) or after a line that opens a block,
ending in "{" or ":" (-2.2). A plain line-numbered listing is the case it is built around;
the offsets are minor.

The program tracks only the previous line and the line so far, and resets them at
each new document.
"""

import re

READS = ()

NUMBERED = re.compile(r"[ \t]*\d+\t")  # a listing line: padding, line number, tab
GUTTER = re.compile(r"[ \t]*\d*")  # the line so far is still inside the line-number gutter
COMMENT = re.compile(r"\s*(//|/\*|\*|#)")  # previous line is a comment or doc line
OPENER = re.compile(r"[{:]\s*$")  # previous line opens a block


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[2] != doc:
        prev, line = "", ""
    else:
        prev, line = carry[0], carry[1]

    parts = tok.split("\n")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        start, seg, before = line, tok, prev  # token continues the current line
        new_prev, new_line = prev, line + tok
    else:
        completed = line + parts[0] if len(parts) == 2 else parts[-2]
        start, seg, before = "", parts[-1], completed  # token starts a new line
        new_prev, new_line = completed, parts[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if seg and not seg.strip() and start == "":  # indentation that starts a line
        if NUMBERED.match(before):
            value = 7.7
        elif COMMENT.match(before):
            value = 2.3
        elif OPENER.search(before):
            value = -2.2
    elif seg.isdigit() and NUMBERED.match(before) and GUTTER.fullmatch(start):
        value = 1.0  # a digit of the line number
    return (new_prev, new_line, doc), value

"""Silent at each document's first token; slightly negative on verbs of wanting or seeking.

This component is a single direction of layer 15's MLP hidden state, dominated by hidden
unit 844 (a SiLU(gate) * up product). Its activation is diffuse: it has mean 0.02 and
standard deviation 0.35, and token identity, short word windows, repetition, position and
script explain almost none of it. The one lexical lean found in the training rows is that
the strongly negative values fall on intention verbs ("wanted", "decided", "seeking",
"aiming", "want"). Those tokens get a small negative value; every other token gets the
average, +0.02. At a document's first token the activation is about zero, so the program
predicts zero there.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN = 0.02
INTENT_VERBS = {"want", "wanted", "wanting", "wants", "decided", "seeking", "aiming"}
INTENT_VALUE = -0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in INTENT_VERBS:
        return carry, INTENT_VALUE
    return carry, MEAN

"""p-82af68dd@100000 / layers.15.mlp.down_proj : component 845.

What this component is. It is one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. Its
input direction V_845 is almost entirely the MLP hidden unit 845 (weight 0.54 on that unit,
about 0.01 to 0.07 on each of the others), so its activation is about 0.54 times that
hidden unit's value plus a sum of many small terms. Its output direction U_845 has no
clear readable meaning on the unembedding.

What it responds to. Nothing we could name. Its activation is heavy-tailed (sd 0.30, RMS
0.30, largest |value| 5.5): about 1% of positions carry almost half of the variance. The
large values are not tied to a token type, a repeated or copied span, a position in the
document, a column in the line, a document, or a rare or frequent token. Token identity,
previous-token identity and simple token classes all explain under 1% of its variance on
held-out rows.

So the best short program predicts its mean everywhere. That is the only prediction this
analysis supports.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.03  # measured mean over the eval rows, about 0.029


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's typical activation at this position: a constant."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 847: a near-constant, context-free activation.

What it is: its activation is (MLP hidden vector . V_847) * ||U_847||, a weighted sum over
the layer's 6144 hidden units. One unit, neuron 847 of layer 15, has the largest single
weight (0.17) and carries about 37% of the covariance with the activation (correlation 0.55);
the other units carry the rest, spread thin.

Why no readable trigger: neuron 847 is contextual, not lexical. Knowing the current token
explains about 2% of its variance on held-out text, the previous token about 1%, and position
in the document, or whether the token or bigram already appeared, almost nothing. Its largest
values come from test-runner logs ("--- PASS", "=== RUN") and tool-response tags, but those
contexts are too rare to move the variance.

So this program predicts the component's typical value everywhere, its mean, about 0.033.
It explains essentially none of the variance, and its effect on the model's outputs matches
switching the component off, which is itself negligible.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.033


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's mean activation at every position."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 848: a near-unpredictable, near-zero signal.

What the component is: its input direction reads MLP hidden unit 848 of layer 15
most strongly (weight 0.48 of its unit-norm-0.85 input vector), so its activation
is that unit's value scaled by a fixed factor. The value is a diffuse,
context-dependent signal: most of its variance sits within each token type, and
it is near zero on average. Measured out of sample, no readable concept explains
it: token identity (about 2%), the previous token, the next token, position in
the document, character class, negation words and document genre each explain
under about 3% of its variance.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical activation, a
constant 0.05 (its mean over ordinary positions), and 0 at the first token of
each document, where the activation is essentially always 0. It does not track
when the component is large (its largest values, such as on "not", "wrong" or
"change", are not predictable from the prefix).
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = 0.05  # mean activation over ordinary positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    first = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first else TYPICAL

"""Constant predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 849.

What the component does: almost nothing. Its causal importance is essentially
zero everywhere (it never passes the 0.1 harvest threshold in 10M tokens), and
switching it off changes the model's next-token distribution by ~2e-6 nats.

What its activation looks like: a diffuse signal with mean ~0.11 and std ~0.32,
both signs occur, and no simple concept explains it. Token identity explains
under 1% of its variance out of sample; character class (letter, digit,
punctuation, space), position in the document and leading-space status explain
about 1% or less. It is only weakly persistent from one token to the next
(lag-1 correlation ~0.4), so it tracks something about the surrounding text
that a readable rule cannot capture.

So this program predicts the component's mean activation at every position.
That gets variance explained of about 0, and keeps the output essentially
unchanged.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.11  # mean over sampled positions (eval mean is 0.111)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # Same value at every position; no state is carried between tokens.
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Predicts the average activation of component 850 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj.

What the component is: its input direction is almost entirely the layer-15 MLP hidden unit
850 (0.53 of its 0.85 norm sits on that unit), so its activation is roughly that unit's value
times a fixed scale (corr about 0.6). That unit is set by the residual stream in context,
not by the current token: no token identity, token class (digits, CJK, punctuation, words),
repeat-of-earlier-token flag or position in the document predicts it on held-out text
(each explains under 2% of its variance). Its output direction has no clear token meaning,
and it is effectively unused by the model (switching it off changes next-token predictions
by about 2e-6 nats).

What this program does: since nothing readable in the prefix predicts the activation, it
predicts the component's mean value, -0.037, at every position. That reproduces the
activation's average and explains none of its variance.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.037


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation predicted at this position: the mean, whatever the prefix says."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Explain layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 852 (a rank-one piece of the layer-15 MLP output).

What the component does: its output direction, read through the tied unembedding, promotes
travel and motion words ("travel", "traveled", "travels", "rotation", "slides"). Its
activation is large and positive mostly in narrative passages about moving or getting
somewhere, and is strongest on the verbs of travel, transport and placement themselves
("drove", "travelled", "flew", "reached", "located", "placed"). Most of its variance is
spread over ordinary tokens with no simple cue, so this program captures only the
strongest, most readable part: travel and location verbs get a positive activation,
everything else gets zero.

Measured on training text, these verbs average about +0.5 (against about -0.01 overall),
but they are rare, so the program explains only a sliver of the variance; a token-identity
table would explain at most a few percent more.
"""

READS = ()

# Verbs of travel, transport and placing something somewhere.
TRAVEL_VERBS = {
    "drove", "drive", "driving", "driven",
    "travel", "travels", "traveled", "travelled", "traveling", "travelling",
    "flew", "fly", "flying", "flown",
    "ride", "rode", "riding", "ridden",
    "sail", "sailed", "sailing",
    "walked", "walking", "speeding", "sped", "transported", "transport",
    "moved", "moving",
    "located", "reached", "placed", "positioned", "parked",
}

ACTIVE_VALUE = 0.5  # typical activation on those verbs


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: positive on travel and location verbs, else zero."""
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, (ACTIVE_VALUE if word in TRAVEL_VERBS else 0.0)

"""Predict the component's average activation everywhere.

Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:853 writes a small, dense signal into the residual
stream. Its activation is a linear read of many of layer 15's MLP hidden units (mostly
units 853 and 211), with no simple token, character-class, position or document pattern:
token identity explains about 2% of its variance, a token-category rule about 0.1%, and
position in the document nothing. Its causal importance is essentially zero everywhere,
so it does not change the model's output. The best readable prediction is therefore its
mean, about 0.009, with no dependence on the prefix.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0089


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15, MLP unit 854 (the down_proj component's one rank-one piece), read as its activation.

Plain-language reading: this unit is a "we are inside a run of Chinese, Japanese or Korean
text" signal that grows with the run. Each CJK token in a row adds to it, saturating after
about eight tokens, so it is strongest in long stretches of dense CJK prose (mid-sentence)
and resets to zero at the first non-CJK token, such as Latin text, digits, spaces or
punctuation. Its activation is near zero everywhere else.

The only state is the length of the current CJK run, reset at each new document.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

CJK = regex.compile(r"[\p{Han}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Hangul}]")
SLOPE = 0.4  # activation added per CJK token in the run
CAP = 8  # the run stops adding after this many tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    run = 0 if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    if CJK.search(token):
        run += 1
        return run, SLOPE * min(run, CAP)
    return 0, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 856: a weak, mostly unexplained signal.

What it does, in plain terms:
- On the first token of each document the component is silent: predict 0.
- Otherwise predict a small negative baseline, -0.03 (its typical value).
- Tokens written in Cyrillic script push it more negative (about -0.11), the one
  readable pattern found. Its hidden unit (layer 15, MLP unit 856) is most negative on
  Russian function words and word endings, such as 'без', 'для', 'этом', 'того'.
- Tokens containing a line break sit slightly above baseline (about 0.0): it is
  positive on answer and heading openings ('Here', 'Summary', '##', 'Perfect').

Why it is this simple: the activation is diffuse. Its spread (0.36) is almost all
within-document and context-dependent. Token identity explains about 2% of the variance
(about 5% for the hidden unit that drives it), and the script and line-break rules
explain about 0.2%. Switched off, the component changes the model's predictions by almost
nothing, so the honest explanation is a weak, mostly noise-like contributor.
"""

import re

READS = ()

BASELINE = -0.03
CYRILLIC_VALUE = -0.11
LINE_BREAK_VALUE = 0.0
CYRILLIC = re.compile(r"[Ѐ-ӿ]")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Position within the current document: the first token of a document is 0.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n = 0
    else:
        n = carry[1] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if n == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif CYRILLIC.search(token):
        value = CYRILLIC_VALUE
    elif "\n" in token:
        value = LINE_BREAK_VALUE
    else:
        value = BASELINE
    return (doc, n), float(value)

"""Layer 15's MLP hidden unit 858, read as a preposition detector.

This component reads one direction in layer 15's MLP hidden space (mostly hidden unit
858, about a fifth of its variance; the rest is spread over many units) and writes into
the residual stream. Its activation is a noisy signal centred near zero, but it is clearly
larger on prepositions
that introduce an object or target, after a verb or noun: "pass these skills TO my
students", "a strong predictor OF", "carried forward TO", "for", "with", "by", "into",

    operators, indented lines, #include, @Override, etc.

    tied to any token: token identity explains nothing on held-out rows.

recent narrative cues (past-tense verbs, third-person pronouns) minus recent code cues
(code symbols, newline-indented lines), decaying over roughly 50 tokens and reset at each
document start. The prediction is a small multiple of that score.

rows). The component's behaviour is diffuse, and no token-level or genre-level rule
tested here explains it.

SCALE = 0.12  # the prediction's size per unit of score
BIAS = 0.035  # the component's mean activation

    "was were had went came saw said took made got felt knew thought looked found told "
    "gave began passed stood sat ran held heard left kept seemed became turned opened "
    "walked".split()
)
THIRD_PERSON = set("he she they his her him them their".split())

def narrative_cue(token):
    """A word that narrates: a past-tense verb or a third-person pronoun."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not regex.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", word):

    past = (word.endswith("ed") and len(word) > 3) or word in IRREGULAR_PAST
    return past or word in THIRD_PERSON


def code_cue(token):
    """Code or markup: a code symbol, or a line break that starts an indented line."""
    return any(c in CODE_SYMBOLS for c in token) or ("\n" in token and not token.strip())

    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != carry[2]:

  sit above average.

  milf, ...) making up a few percent of the document's recent tokens lift the
  activation sharply, most of all on split-word pieces.
- Digits, punctuation and line breaks sit slightly below average.

spread that these rules do not capture (the program explains about 2% of the
variance).

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

ADULT = (
    "porn", "sex", "escort", "milf", "salope", "hentai", "xxx", "nude",
    "webcam", "rencontre", "masturb", "erot", "fuck", "bdsm", "porr",
    "sesso", "секс", "порн", "эрот", "色情", "性爱", "做爱", "少妇", "人妻",
    "自慰", "巨乳", "性交", "乱伦", "情色", "援交",
)

def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = tok.strip()
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    density, piece, cap_run = (0.0, 0, 0) if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    is_adult = any(word in text.lower() for word in ADULT)

context, and token identity explains only a few percent of it, so this program follows only its
crude tendencies:

- the first token of each document is zero;
- a token that already occurred earlier in the same document (repeated code or text) leans more
  positive, except file-extension tokens (".test", ".ts", ".png", ...), which lean negative;
- code-like tokens (identifiers, method names, symbols, brackets) lean slightly positive;
- English words and digits sit near a small positive baseline.

add error. The program explains well under 1% of the variance.

READS = ()

GAIN = 0.4
"""Shrinks every prediction: the best scale for these rules is near 0.4."""

FILE_EXT = re.compile(
    r"\s?\.(test|ts|js|py|png|txt|go|rs|yaml|pdf|json|md|java|tsx|jsx|html|css|xml|csv|sh|lock)"
)
CODE_LIKE = re.compile(r"\s?\.?_*[A-Za-z]*[_A-Z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_]*|\s?\.[A-Za-z]+|[^\w\s]+")

This component is, to good approximation, one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP: its
down_proj column is almost entirely that unit's direction, so its activation is the
unit's value (silu(gate) * up), scaled to about 1. The unit is polysemantic, and most of its
size sits on context-dependent tokens, so a short rule explains only a small part of it.

- Strongly negative on the opening of a chat turn or tool block: <|im_start|>, <think>,
  <tool_call>, <tool_response>. The closing tags and <|im_end|> are near zero.
- Positive on code-comment openers ('#', '//', '/*') and on escaped or literal line breaks
  inside code and strings ('\\n', tab-newline, carriage return, '+\n').
- Negative on code punctuation that follows a value: '->', '{"', "['", '::', '":', '|', '—'.

# Code comment openers: positive.
COMMENTS = {"#", " #", "//", " //", "///", " ///", "/*"}
# Line breaks written as text (escaped or literal) inside code and strings: positive.
LINE_BREAKS = {"\\n", "\t\n", "\r", "+\n"}
# Punctuation that follows a value in code, JSON or markup: negative.
CODE_PUNCT = {
    "->": -1.3, " ->": -1.3, " {\"": -2.4, "['": -1.3, "::": -0.8, "\":": -0.6,
    " |": -0.5, " —": -0.5, "\\t": -0.6,

LINE_BREAK_VALUE = 1.0

This component is almost exactly one MLP hidden unit: its input vector V_c is about 0.82 along

negative on the chat-template role word "assistant" (the strongest single case), on words for a

their expertise ("expert", "professor", "historian", "journalist", "author", "judges"). It is
mildly negative on the pronouns and generic words that point back at such a person ("who",
"he", "his", "someone"). Everywhere else it sits near zero.

most of its large swings sit in contexts no word list reaches: its activation is spread across

Each position is read alone, with no state carried between tokens.

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

ASSISTANT_VALUE = -3.2
"""The "assistant" in a chat template's "<|im_start|>assistant" header."""

CREDENTIAL_VALUE = -0.8
"""Words of expertise, knowledge, experience, perspective, and people named by expertise."""

    r"lawyer|author|writer|historian|journalist|judge|honest|passion|mature|familiar|"
    r"understand|scholar|scientist)"
)

What it does, in plain terms
- Its activation is a fixed linear read-out of the layer-15 MLP hidden state. No single
  neuron, token or token class carries it: predicting it from the current token alone,
  or from the previous token, explains nothing. Its variance is spread over thousands of
  hidden units.
- What little structure there is depends on position inside the current document:
  * the first token of a document (position 0) reads about 0;
  * the second token reads clearly positive (about +0.2), the third and fourth weaker
    positives, and the activation settles to a small negative value (about -0.07) for
    the rest of the document;
  * the document-separator / chat markers (tokens written as <|...|>, such as
    <|endoftext|>) read clearly negative (about -0.6).

change) and returns those values. It explains roughly 0.75% of the variance on the
eval rows (Pearson r about 0.09). Switching the component off already has almost no
effect on the model, so this program is close to the component's own effect.

READS = ()

FIRST_BUMP = 0.3    # extra value at document position 1, decays by 0.6 per token
BASELINE = -0.07    # typical value deeper into a document
MARKER = -0.6       # value at separator / chat-marker tokens such as <|endoftext|>


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Value at the newest token. `carry` is (document id, position in document)."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if pos == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif "<|" in tok:
        value = MARKER
    else:
        value = BASELINE + FIRST_BUMP * 0.6 ** (pos - 1)
    return (doc, pos), value

Mostly near zero. Inside step-by-step reasoning that has hit a dead end
("impossible", "contradiction", "no solution", "Hmm", "Wait"), it goes negative,
most strongly on the sentence or clause break that closes the failed step, and
on the pivot words that open the next thought ("Hmm", "Alternatively", "Therefore").

(the 'stall'), and predicts from it at each break, plus fixed values on pivot words.

READS = ()

BREAKS = {".", ".\n\n", ".\n", ",", ",\n\n"}
DOUBT = {"hmm", "wait", "no", "not", "impossible", "contradiction", "invalid",
         "but", "however", "wrong", "error", "mistake", "cannot", "can't",
         "doesn't", "isn't", "never", "still", "perhaps", "maybe", "alternatively",
         "incorrect", "fail", "problem", "unless", "≠", "⇒"}
PIVOTS = {"hmm", "wait", "alternatively", "therefore", "thus", "hence", "so",
          "however", "but", "maybe", "perhaps", "instead"}
DECAY = 0.95


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    stall, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        stall = 0.0  # a new document starts with no reasoning behind it
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

- Its activation is near zero on almost every token, but it spikes on tokens that are a

  Multi-character Chinese words (现代化, 利率, 自动驾驶) and everything non-Chinese sit
  near zero.
- The size of the spike depends on the surrounding text: it is large when the document
  so far is dense in one-character Chinese words (terse, classical or folk-style prose,
  e.g. 三国-style narrative or fortune-telling text), and small in modern prose.

The program therefore keeps a running density of one-character Chinese tokens in the
current document (an exponential moving average, about 20 tokens long, reset at each
new document). For a token that is one Chinese character, it predicts
5 * density - 0.8; for every other token it predicts -0.06, the typical resting level.

sample it was tuned on, and 1.7% on the eval rows (Pearson r 0.18). Its heavy tail
(a few large spikes carry most of the variance) makes the share noisy. A token-identity
lookup table reaches about 8%, and perfect predictions on single-character tokens would
reach about 34%, so most of the component's variance is a context-dependent spike the
program does not capture. Keyword cues from dictionary glosses (ghost, fate, god...)
and a traditional-versus-simplified split added nothing.

READS = ()

REST = -0.06  # typical activation on ordinary tokens
ALPHA = 0.05  # how quickly the running density forgets older tokens (~20 tokens)


def is_single_han(text):
    """True when the token holds exactly one Chinese (Han) character."""
    return len(regex.findall(r"\p{Han}", text)) == 1

    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])

        density = 0.0  # a new document starts with no history
    else:
        density = carry[0]
    single = is_single_han(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = 5.0 * density - 0.8 + REST if single else REST
    density = (1 - ALPHA) * density + ALPHA * (1.0 if single else 0.0)
    return (density, doc), float(value)

-0.013). Almost none of its variance follows any readable rule. The only regularities
found, measured on about 4M training tokens, are by kind of token:

- digits, and indentation (spaces or tabs with no newline), sit a little below zero;
- newline whitespace and lowercase words with no leading space sit a bit lower than
  average;
- Han characters and ordinary words after a space sit near zero.

which has no context and reads as zero. It explains only a few tenths of a percent of the

    "digit": -0.054,
    "indent": -0.056,
    "newline": -0.028,
    "word": -0.028,
    "word_space": -0.001,
    "han": 0.006,
    "other": -0.005,

"""Disjunction detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 890.

The component fires on the word "or" when it joins two alternatives ("3 or 4",
"tea or coffee"), in English and in other languages. Its strongest trigger is
mid-sentence " or" with its leading space; the same word in other languages
("oder", "ou", "eller", "или", "或", "hoặc", "atau", ...) fires about as strongly.
Capitalised "Or"/"OR", "nor", and other languages' words that are less common
or less exact fire less. Looser alternative-introducers ("Alternatively",
"Otherwise", "Either") fire weakly. Everything else is predicted as zero.

Values are rounded averages of the component's activation on each group in a
training sample: about 4 for the strong group, 2 for the medium, 1 for the weak.
The program explains only the disjunction-shaped part of the activation: the
rest of its variance is a diffuse background with no simple token pattern.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

STRONG = {" or", " oder", " ou", " eller", " или", " أو", " atau", " hoặc", " vagy", "或", "或是", " 或", "或者"}
MEDIUM = {" Or", " OR", "Or", " nor", " lub", " veya", " ó", "_or", "还是", "還是", "または", "หร", " sau", " bzw"}
WEAK = {" Alternatively", " Otherwise", " Either", " Nor"}
LEVEL = {**{w: 4.0 for w in STRONG}, **{w: 2.0 for w in MEDIUM}, **{w: 1.0 for w in WEAK}}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):

"""Copula detector: fires on forms of "be", and on the word right after one.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:892 writes into the residual
stream at the MLP's output. Its activation is large where the model sits in a
"be" predicate slot, waiting for a complement: a passive participle, an adjective
or a noun phrase ("was held", "is useful", "can be seen").

- On the verb itself it is strong: "been" and "were" and "was" most, then "be",
  "are", "is", "being", and the contractions 'm and 're. "'s" after a pronoun
  ("it's", "he's") is "is" too, and gets a moderate value.
- On an adverb or "not" right after a be-form ("is not", "is often", "was also"),
  the slot is still open, so it stays fairly high.
- After an expletive or deictic subject ("there is", "here are", "this is", "what
  was") it is weaker: those are mostly presentational, not passives.
- Capitalised forms ("Is", "Are") are about half as strong; a be-form with no
  leading space ("\\nis", "(is") is ignored, as it is not an ordinary verb here.
- Everywhere else it sits near zero, with small noise.
"""

READS = ()

BE_VALUE = {
    "is": 8.0, "are": 8.5, "was": 10.3, "were": 10.7, "be": 10.2,
    "been": 11.7, "being": 8.1, "am": 4.1,
    "'m": 5.1, "’m": 6.1, "'re": 5.5, "’re": 6.2,
}
PRONOUNS = {"it", "he", "she", "that", "what", "this"}
AFTER_BE = {
    "not", "also", "often", "typically", "usually", "then", "never", "now",
    "always", "only", "still", "currently", "actually", "generally", "widely",
    "originally", "later", "therefore", "just", "probably", "simply", "clearly",
    "subsequently", "primarily", "commonly", "officially", "initially",
}
EXPLETIVE = {"there", "here", "this", "what"}
AFTER_BE_VALUE = 6.0
EXPLETIVE_FACTOR = 0.4
CAPITAL_FACTOR = 0.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    spaced = raw.startswith(" ")  # "is" after a space; "\nis" or "(is" behave differently
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    prev_is_be = prev in BE_VALUE or prev in ("'s", "’s")

    if word in BE_VALUE and (spaced or not word.isalpha()):
        value = BE_VALUE[word]
        if raw.strip()[:1].isupper():
            value *= CAPITAL_FACTOR
        if prev in EXPLETIVE:
            value *= EXPLETIVE_FACTOR
    elif word in ("'s", "’s"):
        value = 4.0 if prev in PRONOUNS else 0.0
    elif word in AFTER_BE and prev_is_be:
        value = AFTER_BE_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 894: a near-dormant, mostly unexplained direction.

What it is: a rank-one piece of the MLP down projection that reads the MLP's hidden
activations (mostly hidden unit 894 of layer 15, plus a diffuse set of small weights).
Its activation has mean ~0.04, spread ~0.29, and both signs; it almost never matters
(causal importance is ~0 everywhere), and switching it off barely changes the output.

What this program does: it has no real model of the component. It predicts a small
value from the current token's word class: connecting words and prepositions that
open a phrase ("and", "with", "when", "than", "before", "through", ...) get a small
positive value, copulas and pronouns ("is", "was", "it", "to", ...) a small negative
value, and everything else the mean. Token identity explains almost none of the
variance (a per-token lookup table over the top 5000 tokens reaches ~2%), so this
program is expected to explain about 0.2% of it. Its value is in being readable, and
in showing that the component carries little token-level signal.
"""

READS = ()

CONNECTIVES = {
    " and", " with", " when", " than", " through", " before", " after", " by",
    " from", " each", " other", " already", " again", " back", " new", ",", " the", " a",
}
COPULAS = {" is", " was", " are", " be", " it", " It", " but", " should", " to"}
CONNECTIVE_VALUE = 0.1
COPULA_VALUE = -0.03
MEAN_VALUE = 0.04


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's predicted activation at the newest token."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position]
    if token in CONNECTIVES:
        return carry, CONNECTIVE_VALUE
    if token in COPULAS:
        return carry, COPULA_VALUE
    return carry, MEAN_VALUE

"""Word-continuation detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 895.

Plain-terms reading: the component goes strongly negative on a token that finishes or
extends a word which the tokenizer has split into several pieces. The piece is a letter
run with no leading space that directly follows another letter run, such as "ATION" in
"OBSERV|ATION", "ge" in "Privileg|e", or "ds" in "CAR|DS". Its size is largest inside
all-caps words or after an all-caps piece (acronyms, identifiers), and smaller for
mixed-case pieces. Word starts, spaces, punctuation and digits are near zero, and so are
CJK pieces, which the component ignores.

The program needs only the current token and the one before it, plus the document label
to reset at each document's first token. The two values are the mean activations of the
two classes, measured on about 520k training tokens. On the eval rows it explains about
12% of the activation's variance (Pearson r 0.35), and it moves the model's next-token
predictions by about 80% of what switching the component off does. Most of the remaining
variance is idiosyncratic: a lookup table of token pairs explains only about 17% on
held-out tokens, so a table would add little, and the conceptual rule gives up little.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

PIECE = regex.compile(r"\p{L}+")
LETTER_END = regex.compile(r"\p{L}$")
HAN = regex.compile(r"\p{Han}")

STRONG = -2.9  # continuation piece in an all-caps word or after an all-caps piece
WEAK = -1.2  # other continuation piece of a split word
NEUTRAL = 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, NEUTRAL
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    continues = bool(PIECE.fullmatch(token)) and bool(LETTER_END.search(prev))
    if not continues or HAN.search(token) or HAN.search(prev):
        return carry, NEUTRAL
    if token.isupper() or prev.isupper():
        return carry, STRONG
    return carry, WEAK
